overview: This event ties together night environment and lighting setup, night emergencies and electrical degradation, and local night procedures in a way that should already make sense before you step. You should be ready to brief what changes the plan, what numbers matter, and where the usual errors start once the workload climbs.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items

children.text: Know the operational purpose, the pilot-visible cues, and the follow-on actions or limits tied to Night Flying Considerations.
Know the operational purpose, the pilot-visible cues, and the follow-on actions or limits tied to Night VFR Chart Interpretation.
Must be used whenever the aircraft is in motion at night.
Aerobatics, short breaks, stalls, and formation flights are prohibited at night.
Touch and go’s to uncontrolled airfields may be conducted provided they have night lighting and a wildlife mitigation pass is conducted prior to operations.
Loss of generator power = no charging of battery.
Loss of generator power = no charging of battery.

items.text: Local Night Sop matters because it changes what you brief, what you look for in the cockpit, or what the next safe decision needs to be.

children.text: Aircraft must not operate within a SIGMET at night unless equipped with operable radar capable of detecting/avoiding isolated thunderstorms.

studyNotes.summary: Have Night Environment and Lighting Setup, plus Night Emergencies and Electrical Degradation organized before step so the cockpit workload never outruns the brief.
